answer: In an agent marketplace trading opal, each seller must lock a fixed bond in a vault before accepting jobs. The bond stays frozen for 30 days after the seller’s last delivery, and cryptographic proof of double billing triggers its forfeiture. At dawn, the market releases only bonds whose waiting period has ended. An attacker running 1,000 fake sellers must fund 1,000 bonds, bear the cost of locked capital, and lose bonds for provable fraud.
